rules.title: missing default-fail
rules.why_flagged: control construct with no terminating failure branch
rules.flag_condition: flag a switch block with no default: label, an if/else-if chain with no terminating else, a state machine assigning a state variable with no invalid-state trap, and a function whose declared error path returns a success-like 0. All four are block-shaped, not line-shaped; the pattern anchors the block and the validator reads it

rules.title: unvalidated encryption result
rules.why_flagged: cryptographic operation whose output is used without being checked
rules.flag_condition: flag when the result is used or emitted with no verify-after-sign or decrypt-after-encrypt check. A glitched signature that is never re-verified is the classic fault-injection primitive

rules.title: single critical decision
rules.why_flagged: security-critical action reached through one decision
rules.flag_condition: flag a single if whose body performs unlock/grant/erase/boot/write-key with no second, independent check. One skipped branch is one glitch

rules.title: unvalidated loop count
rules.why_flagged: loop over a secret with no post-loop iteration-count check
rules.flag_condition: flag loops that compare, copy, hash or clear a secret/key/MAC buffer and have no post-loop `if (i != n)` check. The pattern matches every loop on purpose: narrowing it to loops that mention a key on the same line would drop the loops whose buffer is named on the line above, and a hit this rule never took cannot be recovered downstream

rules.title: plain security booleans
rules.why_flagged: security state held in a plain boolean, one bit-flip from the wrong answer
rules.flag_condition: flag security decisions carried in a plain bool/int rather than a sparse, redundant or complemented value. The keyword must be a whole word or an underscore-delimited part of one: an earlier form used \w*(ok|pass)\w*, which matched token_count, lookahead and bypass_count

rules.title: unverified sensitive value
rules.why_flagged: value read from NVM, flash, OTP, fuses or EEPROM
rules.flag_condition: flag when the value feeds a security decision with no CRC, MAC, parity or shadow-copy verification. Non-volatile storage is writable by an attacker who holds the device

rules.title: missing CFI counter
rules.why_flagged: multi-step security sequence with no control-flow integrity counter
rules.flag_condition: flag a multi-step security function (verify then derive then unlock, or measure then compare then boot) with no monotonically-updated flow counter or step token validated at the end. Whether the steps are present is a block-shaped judgement the pattern cannot make; the pattern anchors the candidate function and the validator reads the sequence

rules.title: unbounded sensitive output
rules.why_flagged: length of an outbound transfer may come from the request
rules.flag_condition: flag when the length comes from a request field while the source is a key, secret or RAM buffer, with no clamp to the actual secret length. This is the Heartbleed shape with a device on the other end

rules.title: non-constant-time comparison
rules.why_flagged: secret compared byte-by-byte with an early exit
rules.flag_condition: also flag an early return or break inside a comparison loop. HW-009 assumes the attacker holds the device and power analysis is available; LOG-008 is the same defect asked about remote timing. The scout emits both either way

rules.title: raw key material
rules.why_flagged: key bytes held, copied or printed in the clear
rules.flag_condition: flag key bytes in plain locals or globals, keys copied with memcpy, keys printed or logged, and keys passed by value across a module boundary, where no key handle or slot API (psa_key_id_t, ATCA_KEY_ID, keyslot) is used. The presence of a handle API is what disqualifies this, and it is not on the same line, so there is no skip path

rules.title: software crypto
rules.why_flagged: hand-written or bundled software crypto in application code
rules.flag_condition: flag when a hardware engine or a vetted library is available in-tree. Software crypto on a device an attacker holds leaks through power and EM whatever the algorithm is

rules.title: zero-offset access/clearing
rules.why_flagged: secret cleared or walked from index 0 with a plain loop
rules.flag_condition: the memset may be optimised away entirely - look for explicit_bzero, memset_s, OPENSSL_cleanse or a volatile pointer instead. A zero-offset sequential walk over key material is also the easiest trace to align for a side-channel attack
